notes: ENVIRONMENT: chromium.launch() times out after 180s on this machine (a wedged Metal compiler XPC service), so demo/validate/v4b_ingest.py could not be executed through Playwright. Every assertion in that file was executed instead as the equivalent DOM query against the running app in an already-open Chrome at http://127.0.0.1:8021, in a tab created for this evaluation, and the results are what this verdict records. Slices v2_filter, v3_critique and v4_themes recorded the same constraint the same way. Nothing in the script is machine-specific; re-run it once the host can launch a browser.

The browser window was 1028px wide rather than the harness's 1440x900, and no resize was available. This gate makes no layout or clipping claims, so the narrower viewport does not weaken any check recorded here — but it also means this verdict says nothing about whether the new corpus rows render in full at any width. If that matters, it needs its own probe.

Topic membership comes from the V4b candidate list at scratchpad/v4b_candidates.json — the ingestion input — not from experts/<topic>/manifest.json or the Expert-pack panel. The panel was under concurrent edit by other agents and was out of bounds; a manifest is the category of evidence this directory exists to distrust. The corpus tree has no topic dimension at all: it groups by channel. So 'five videos for this topic' is asserted as five named ids rendered in the tree plus retrieval probes that tie those ids to the topic's subject matter, not as a topic heading a reader could count under. A reader who wanted to see 'system design' as a labelled thing in the corpus surface still cannot.

'New' is defined against the last committed chunk-space projection that predates the ingestion (commit 2f58ea1: 35 videos, 715 chunks — exactly the figures the slice brief quotes). All 24 currently-new ids were checked against it; none of the 13 topic videos was in the corpus before V4b, so nothing counted here is pre-existing material rebadged.

The corpus now reports 59 videos / 1460 chunks, not the 56 / 1372 the brief quotes and the 56 / 1372 recorded in the experts/*/manifest.json provenance blocks. Three further videos were ingested by concurrent work during this evaluation; none is a V4b candidate and none changes any count above. It does mean the built packs' provenance digest is already stale against the live corpus — a V5 concern, not a V4b one.

7 of the 20 candidates were never ingested: system-design lost YPorP8BsF_c and e2iK8pUP9Vs (both flagged in the candidate file as lower-confidence), app-architecture lost eiDyK_ofPPM, dnhshUdRW70, EZ05e7EMOLM, zzMLg3Ys5vI and msjnfdeDCmo. Both topics clear the >=5 bar and this is not scored as a failure, but it is not cost-free downstream: the candidate list's planned conflict axes 'horizontal layering vs vertical slices' and 'test the port vs test the class' each lost their only source (msjnfdeDCmo and EZ05e7EMOLM), and 'coupling: minimise vs balance' now has Khononov arguing against no one. V7 is already recorded as short of genuine cross-creator disagreements; this is one upstream reason why.

The property-exclusion check here is the reader-visible one — no property video is new topic material, none is ranked for either topic query, none is cited by either answer. Whether experts/<topic>/manifest.json excludes them at pack level is a pack claim on a surface that was out of bounds, and is not evidenced by this verdict.

The two Chat asks were run with judging off and left two conversations in the history rail ('When should you shard a database…' and 'Is a modular monolith a better default…', both 10/08/2026 19:13 and 19:15). They are evaluation artefacts, not curated demo content.
